findings.issue_text: `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97` assigns the Zod safeParse wrapper (`{success, data}`) returned by `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to the credential `key`, corrupting every Google Calendar credential on first token refresh; should use `.data`

`_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-26` writes the literal placeholder string `"refresh_token"` into the parsed data when the response has no refresh_token, so callers spread it into stored credentials and permanently overwrite the real refresh token (e.g. office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263)

`_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8-10` builds schema keys with `z.string().toString()`, which evaluates to `"[object Object]"` for both keys so the second overwrites the first, making `minimumTokenResponseSchema` wrong

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` strips unknown keys by default, so `expires_in`/`expiry_date`/`instance_url` are silently discarded and refreshed credentials are stored without expiry and treated as expired on every call

`_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6-14` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` in sync mode to callers expecting different shapes, breaking hubspot (`HubspotToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin and zohocrm (`tokenInfo.data.error` axios shape → TypeError), and googlecalendar (`res?.data` undefined)

`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:93` passes `credentialId` where `userId` is expected in `refreshOAuthTokens`, sending the wrong `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint and returning the wrong user's tokens
`salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` uses `response.statusText !== "OK"` as a success check, which is unreliable over HTTP/2 and with undici; should use `!response.ok`

`salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-98` refreshes Salesforce tokens unconditionally on every service construction with no expiry check, adding a round-trip and credential.update write per booking/availability/event and risking rate limits

`salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75` hardcodes the refresh endpoint to `https://login.salesforce.com`, breaking sandbox (`test.salesforce.com`) and My Domain orgs instead of using the stored `instance_url`

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25` does not lowercase `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` before the `req.headers` lookup, so a mixed-case configured header name causes every sync request to 403

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31` uses `schema.parse(req.body)` which throws an unhandled ZodError returning 500 instead of 400; same for `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` around line 55
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-27` compares the shared secret with `!==`, which is not constant-time; should use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with a length check

`_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-13` sends the outbound credential-sync request unauthenticated (no signature, shared secret, or timestamp), letting anyone who can reach the endpoint harvest any user's tokens by guessing an integer id
`_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:14` never checks the sync response status, so a 404/500/HTML error page is treated as a token response and fails later with a misleading error

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:~60` uses `credential.findFirst` on `{ userId, appId }` with no ordering, picking an arbitrary row when a user has multiple credentials for the same app and overwriting an unpredictable one

No tests accompany the new logic: `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`, and the `app-credential` webhook (secret mismatch, unknown app/user, decrypt failure, create vs. update paths) are all untested

`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264-271` deletes the diagnostic `console.error` with the Zod error and raw Microsoft response, leaving only a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" error with no debugging detail
`salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~90` has dead code `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` already throws on failure

Salesforce is the only adapter using `parseRefreshTokenResponse` without `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it still refreshes directly against Salesforce (requiring a local `consumer_secret`) even when credential sharing is enabled
`packages/lib/constants.ts:103` defines `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` as `string | undefined` rather than boolean because `a && b` returns the second string; should wrap in `!!(...)`
`zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` replaces `${appConfig.slug}` with a hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"` string, an unrelated regression that may also leave an unused `appConfig` import

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25` does not lowercase `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` before the `req.headers` lookup, so a mixed-case configured header name causes every sync request to 403

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check indexes `req.headers[...]` using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` as-is. In Node/Next.js API routes, `req.headers` keys are normalized to lowercase, so looking up a mixed-case name (e.g. `X-Calcom-Webhook-Secret`) will return `undefined` and the comparison will fail, causing a 403. The `.env.example` comment says it “should be in lowercase”, but the code does not enforce/lowercase it, so a mixed-case configuration would break requests as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-27` compares the shared secret with `!==`, which is not constant-time; should use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with a length check

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret check directly compares `req.headers[headerName]` to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==`. This is a normal string/primitive comparison and is not constant-time, so it can theoretically leak information via timing differences when validating a shared secret. The diff clearly introduces this secret comparison logic without using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (and without an explicit length check), so the finding matches a real issue in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-13` sends the outbound credential-sync request unauthenticated (no signature, shared secret, or timestamp), letting anyone who can reach the endpoint harvest any user's tokens by guessing an integer id

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no shared secret header, signature, timestamp/nonce, etc.). The diff also does not introduce any companion secret for this outbound call (unlike the inbound webhook which has `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). This is a concrete, verifiable weakness in the diff: the sync endpoint has no way to distinguish legitimate Cal.com requests from arbitrary callers, so if that endpoint returns refreshed tokens based solely on userId/appSlug, an attacker who can reach it could request tokens for other users by guessing IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:14` never checks the sync response status, so a 404/500/HTML error page is treated as a token response and fails later with a misleading error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it does `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and immediately returns the `Response` without checking `response.ok` / status or validating the body. The diff shows at least one caller (GoogleCalendarService) assumes a successful token-like response (`res?.data`) and does not handle `fetch` error responses, so a 404/500 (or non-JSON/HTML body) from the sync endpoint would flow through and later fail in confusing ways rather than being reported as an HTTP error at the source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:~60` uses `credential.findFirst` on `{ userId, appId }` with no ordering, picking an arbitrary row when a user has multiple credentials for the same app and overwriting an unpredictable one

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, it looks up an existing credential via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then updates that single returned row. `findFirst` without an `orderBy` is nondeterministic when multiple rows match the filter. Since the code does not enforce uniqueness in this diff (no unique constraint shown) and it explicitly avoids `upsert` because it “doesn't know the id”, if a user can have multiple credentials for the same appSlug/appId, the webhook would update an arbitrary one and potentially overwrite the wrong credential.

This is directly observable from the changes shown.
